sections.h2: How can you sell a house in Lombard?
sections.html:
Lombard sellers choose between a traditional listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale, and a cash purchase of the house as-is. The village, in DuPage County, runs permitting and code enforcement through its Community Development Department, and deeds are recorded by the DuPage County Recorder, so those two offices set most of the practical timeline.

The 2020 census counted 44,476 people in Lombard, making it the largest of the four Illinois places in this batch of pages, and the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate is 44,399.

Lombard began as Babcock's Grove, named for early settlers on the DuPage River, and took its present name from a Chicago developer who mapped the settlement in 1868. The Galena and Chicago Union Railroad arrived in 1848, and the village incorporated in 1869. A farm family settled on 80 acres in 1837, and their house, since restored by the Lombard Historical Society, was added to the National Park Service's Network to Freedom list of Underground Railroad sites in 2011.

The village calls itself the Lilac Village. A colonel's estate left to the village in 1927 became Lilacia Park, with some 200 varieties of lilac, and the Lilac Time festival and parade have run since 1930 into mid-May. A house near the park or the downtown station can use that identity in its listing description.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers show about Lombard housing?
sections.html:
Lombard has the highest median rent and the highest median home value among the four places in this comparison, and the shortest commute. It also has the largest share of residents with a bachelor's degree.

With 70.8 percent owner occupancy, rental housing is a larger part of Lombard than of the other three places. The short commute reflects the Metra Union Pacific West Line station, the I-88 and I-355 corridors and Illinois Routes 38, 53, 56 and 64. Pace buses use Yorktown Center as a hub, and the Illinois Prairie Path and Great Western Trail run through on former rail lines.

sections.h2: What is the local economy doing for home values?
sections.html:
The village's fiscal year 2024 financial report cites a 9.79 percent increase in equalized assessed valuation, with new construction adding $5.06 million. Retail, manufacturing, hospitality and professional services anchor the economy, and redevelopment projects near Yorktown Center include Lilac Station, Yorktown Reserve and the Summit at Yorktown. Retail sales per capita reached $27,321 in 2022 on the Census table.

Assessed value is one input to property tax bills, so ask the DuPage County Treasurer and Supervisor of Assessments for your parcel's current numbers before you set a price.

sections.h2: Which Lombard schools do buyers ask about?
sections.html:
Lombard's public high schools belong to Glenbard Township High School District 87, shared with Glen Ellyn, and Glenbard East High School is in the village. Elementary and middle schools (kindergarten through grade 8) belong to Lombard School District 44 or DuPage School District 45, depending on the street. Private choices include Montini Catholic High School and the College Preparatory School of America.

Line up the elementary district for your address before the first showing, since it shapes which families look at the house.

sections.h2: What permits and code rules apply in Lombard?
sections.html:
The Building Division handles signs, fire, fill and grade, new buildings, additions, backyard chickens, accessory structures and alterations. Permits can be requested online through the village portal, fees are paid when the permit is ready for pickup, and some items such as residential driveways, fences and new roofs carry flat rates. The division's number is (630) 620-5750.

  • Fences and grading: a permit is required for all fences and for all grading.
  • Exterior upkeep: grass and weeds must stay under eight inches during the growing season, and litter must be cleared within seven days.
  • Vehicles: inactive vehicles must be garaged and RVs may not sit in the front yard from November 1 through March 31.
  • Rentals: owners who rent must supply heat at 68 degrees from September 15 through June 1.
  • Address numbers: they must be visible and legible from the street.

A walk-through for these items before listing can head off an inspector's note. Lombard is a non-home-rule municipality with a council-manager government, so check the village code for local rules before you assume a state rule is the only one.

sections.h2: How does recording work with the DuPage County Recorder?
sections.html:
The DuPage County Recorder maintains the county's land records back to 1839, and recording is fee-funded. The posted fee for a deed (Document Class 1) is $86, which the schedule says includes $10 for document storage, $21 for GIS, $1 for the real property fee and $18 for the Rental Housing Support Program. The Recorder's office number is 630-407-5400.

Illinois law (35 ILCS 200/31-10) taxes the transfer at 50 cents per $500 of value or fraction, and 35 ILCS 200/31-25 requires a declaration signed by at least one seller and one buyer. Collection of the tax runs through the recorder, and the statute provides that paper revenue stamps phase out by December 31, 2025, with electronic stamps or other indicia after that. Ask your closing agent whether the village or county adds any local fee on your parcel.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale suit a Lombard owner?
sections.html: A cash sale suits owners who need to sell a house with deferred repairs, a tenant situation or an inherited estate without staging and showings. With median rent near $1,948, landlords holding an older Lombard rental sometimes prefer a clean exit over renovating. Ask any buyer for a written closing date and a list of who pays each recording item before you sign.

faqs.q: Which office records my deed in Lombard?
faqs.a: The DuPage County Recorder, whose records start in 1839. The posted deed fee includes storage, GIS, real property and Rental Housing Support Program amounts. Call 630-407-5400 for questions.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a new fence?
faqs.a: Yes. Lombard's code enforcement guide says permits are required for all fences so the homeowner knows the requirements before buying the fence. Fences are among the flat-rate permits.

faqs.q: Can I park an RV in my front yard in winter?
faqs.a: No. RVs are not permitted in the front yard from November 1 through March 31, and vehicles that are not street ready must be garaged.
Glenbard East High School in Lombard belongs to Glenbard Township High School District 87. Elementary students attend Lombard School District 44 or DuPage School District 45 depending on the street.

faqs.q: What is the Illinois transfer tax rate?
faqs.a: It is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500 stated in the declaration, under 35 ILCS 200/31-10. A mortgage the buyer takes the property subject to is excluded from the base.
